questions.q: What is the karyotype notation for a male with Down syndrome caused by free trisomy 21?
questions.a: The correct karyotype is 47,XY,+21. A wrong answer like 46,XY,+21 reveals the student thinks the total chromosome count remains 46 (missing that an extra chromosome increases the total). Writing 47,XX,+21 confuses sex chromosomes, showing they don't understand the notation separates total count, sex chromosomes, and abnormality.

questions.q: Explain why maternal age over 35 years is a risk factor for Down syndrome, but paternal age is not significantly associated.
questions.a: Oocytes arrest in prophase I from fetal life until ovulation; prolonged arrest weakens spindle apparatus and cohesion proteins, increasing non-disjunction risk with age. Spermatogenesis is continuous throughout adult life, so no similar aging mechanism exists. A wrong answer citing "older eggs have more mutations" confuses chromosomal non-disjunction with point mutations, showing lack of understanding of meiotic arrest.

questions.q: A couple has a child with Down syndrome. The mother is 28 years old. Karyotyping reveals the child has 46 chromosomes but shows a Robertsonian translocation between chromosomes 14 and 21. The father's karyotype is normal. What is the mother's likely karyotype and the recurrence risk for future pregnancies?
questions.a: Mother's karyotype: 45,XX,rob(14;21)(q10;q10). She is a balanced carrier with 45 chromosomes. Recurrence risk: ~10-15% (theoretical 1/3 for unbalanced gametes, but empirical data shows 10-15% liveborn risk due to selective disadvantage of trisomy 21 conceptuses). A wrong answer of "1 in 800" applies population risk to a translocation case, showing inability to distinguish free trisomy from translocation inheritance.

questions.q: Compare the phenotypic severity and mechanism of free trisomy 21 versus mosaic trisomy 21 (46,XX/47,XX,+21).
questions.a: Free trisomy 21: non-disjunction in meiosis → all cells 47,XX,+21 → full phenotype. Mosaic trisomy 21: post-zygotic non-disjunction in early mitosis → two cell lines (46,XX and 47,XX,+21) → milder/variable phenotype depending on proportion of trisomic cells in critical tissues. A wrong answer stating "mosaic is always milder" ignores tissue-specific distribution; a student saying "mosaic arises from meiosis" confuses timing of non-disjunction.

questions.q: Critique the statement: "Since Down syndrome is caused by an extra chromosome, gene therapy targeting chromosome 21 silencing (like X-inactivation) could cure the condition."
questions.a: Critique: X-inactivation silences one entire X chromosome via XIST RNA; chromosome 21 lacks an XIST-like mechanism and has ~200 genes. Silencing the whole chromosome would disrupt essential genes on the two normal copies. Targeted gene therapy for specific dosage-sensitive genes (e.g., *DYRK1A*) is more plausible but technically unfeasible currently. A wrong answer agreeing shows misunderstanding of X-inactivation specificity and gene dosage sensitivity across a whole chromosome.

questions.q: Design a flowchart for a genetic counselor to differentiate between free trisomy 21, Robertsonian translocation Down syndrome, and mosaic Down syndrome using only karyotype results and parental karyotypes.
questions.a: Flowchart: 1) Child's karyotype: if 47,XX,+21 or 47,XY,+21 → free trisomy (check maternal age). 2) If 46,XX,rob(14;21) or similar → translocation → karyotype parents: if one parent has 45,XX/XY,rob(14;21) → inherited; if both normal → de novo. 3) If two cell lines (e.g., 46,XX/47,XX,+21) → mosaic. A poor flowchart misses parental testing for translocation or doesn't distinguish de novo vs inherited translocation.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Down syndrome (Trisomy 21) is a genetic disorder caused by the presence of an extra copy of chromosome 21, resulting in a total of 47 ______ (karyotype 47,XX,+21 or 47,XY,+21) instead of the normal 46, typically arising from non-disjunction during meiosis.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are a genetic ______ meeting a 38-year-old expectant mother whose ultrasound shows a thickened nuchal fold.
Fill in the blank: She asks, "Why does my age matter, and what exactly is trisomy ______?" Begin by reviewing meiosis: homologous chromosomes separate in Meiosis I, sister chromatids in Meiosis II.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to explain the chromosomal basis of Down syndrome, interpret a karyotype notation (47,XX,+21), correlate maternal age with non-disjunction risk, and list at least five clinical features with their physiological basis.
